Elon Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger would be a ‘good idea’. Committees formed to explore deal

SpaceX is valued at $2 trillion and Tesla at $1.5 trillion. A merger would create one of the largest corporate combinations in history.

Purvi Rajpuria

21 October, 2026 04:13 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

| X: Elon Musk

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Elon Musk on Tuesday said that a merger between his two biggest companies, SpaceX and Tesla, would be a “good idea.”

While the tech billionaire warned that it would be premature to assume the certainty of the merger, he confirmed that special committees had been formed within both companies to examine the move.

Musk has suggested the possibility of a merger between the two companies in the past as well, citing growing overlap between their operations. Last week, British bank Barclays also floated the suggestion that a merger could be announced before Tesla’s annual meeting in December.

Show Full Article

Stock prices for both companies went up after the comment. While shares of SpaceX rose 8 per cent, Tesla’s shares rose 1.8 per cent. The space tech company had also posted its first profit as a public company in the third quarter of this year.

Tesla, an electric car company, is valued at roughly $1.5 trillion. SpaceX, which manufactures space rockets and Starlink internet satellites, is valued at $2 trillion. A combination of the two companies would mark one of the largest mergers in history.

‘Merit in combining the companies’ Musk recently launched Terafab, a combined effort to manufacture computer chips between SpaceX and Tesla. Additionally, SpaceX acquired X and xAI earlier this year, before it went public. Both these moves point to Musk’s attempts at consolidating his companies, signalling that he sees them as operating more effectively when working together.

A full merger between SpaceX and Tesla would make sense considering both companies do work around chips, artificial intelligence, software and more, the BBC reported .

“I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, and there’s a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab obviously, robotics, mass-to-orbit with the Starlink constellation, connectivity,” Musk said.

The merger, however, would ultimately be decided by shareholders. At least 50 per cent of Tesla’s shareholders would need to approve the merger—something Musk has described as “quite a high hurdle to achieve”.

Also read: Ali G is outdated—and that’s why he’s back, writes Sacha Baron Cohen in TIME

Benefits of the merger? With Musk owning just under half of SpaceX and nearly a fifth of Tesla, analysts have said that a merger would give him control of the combined entity, Reuters reported .

Justus Parmar, Chief Executive Officer at Fortuna Investments, pointed to another benefit of bringing SpaceX and Tesla together in one place, for investors to back.

“Tesla runs a high-margin, cash-generative automotive business and there’s more growth to come with the robotaxis on the way. That cash flow could help support SpaceX’s bottom line and fund its very capital-intensive space exploration and launch goals, including orbital data centers,” he said .

(Edited by Ratan Priya)

Cyberattack hits SBI, exposes customer data onto dark web

SBI is investigating the breach after a preliminary analysis identified nearly 4,000 records containing customers’ personal information, the bank said in an exchange filing Wednesday.

Siddhi Nayak

21 October, 2026 03:28 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

State Bank of India, the country’s largest lender by assets, has launched a probe after a suspected cyber attack exposed thousands of customer records containing personal information onto the dark web.

SBI is investigating the breach after a preliminary analysis identified nearly 4,000 records containing customers’ personal information, the bank said in an exchange filing Wednesday. About 375,000 records available on the dark web were analyzed as part of the initial assessment, it said.

The leak highlights cybersecurity risks facing the country’s banking sector as lenders expand digital services and handle increasing volumes of sensitive customer information. In July, state-run Bank of Baroda reported a similar breach.

Show Full Article

“The attack surface from a cyber landscape standpoint is continually changing, giving the extensive technological transformation within financial services primarily account of digitization and AI,” said Vivek Iyer, a partner at Grant Thornton Bharat. Financial institutions not only need to strengthen their cyber posture but also their security operation centers, he said.

The Reserve Bank of India has repeatedly warned lenders about cyber-related risks that could harm financial stability. In a survey of 43 banks and shadow lenders conducted by the central bank, nearly one-third of respondents reported a moderate or significant rise in cyber risks compared to a year earlier.

The concerns are playing across the region. In Japan, a wave of data breaches has hit companies including Daiwa Securities Group Inc., East Japan Railway Co. and SoftBank Corp., prompting government officials to step up cybersecurity measures.

SBI, which is a systemically important bank in India, said the leaked records included customers’ names, registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, email and residential addresses, as well as branch and customer identification numbers and details associated with loan and lead records.

The lender said a detailed investigation is underway to determine the potential source and extent of the exposure, and assess the risks to customers and the bank. The incident has no material impact on SBI’s core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, it said.

Spotify’s big clean-up: 75 million spam songs gone, 50 million hidden

The platform is using listener feedback, metadata and AI-detection tools to keep low-quality tracks out of recommendations.

Triya Gulati

21 October, 2026 03:08 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Representational image | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Spotify has removed more than 75 million songs identified as “slop or spam” from its platform as part of efforts to protect artists and improve the quality of music on the streaming service.

The removed songs were found to have committed “serious or repeated violations” of Spotify’s rules. The company said this in a one-year update on its measures to protect artists, songwriters and producers from the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI).

The platform also filtered out another 50 million tracks from user recommendations following complaints about their quality. Spotify said it examined songs that listeners repeatedly skipped, ignored or flagged as unwanted and found that many were identified as slop or spam.

Show Full Article

“Over the past six months, we’ve made numerous updates to our recommendation system to remove slop and spam, and surface more music made by authentic, human artists. Our editors hold the same standard and don’t program content identified as slop or spam. Since we made these changes, we’ve seen a marked decrease in listener concerns about this content showing up in recommendations,” the company said in a statement from 20 October.

The platform uses listener engagement and feedback, along with upload patterns, metadata and information from third-party AI detection tools to filter out low-quality tracks from recommendations.

However, identifying such content remains a challenge as generative AI technology evolves. Spotify said it was keeping a close watch on tactics such as mass uploads, duplicate tracks, search engine optimisation manipulation, spam-driven playlist networks and artificially short songs.

Spotify said 300,000 artists have now been verified on its platform. Their profiles carry a badge indicating that there is a “real, identifiable person” behind the music. Tracks associated with what Spotify calls “AI Personas” receive a separate label.

By default, AI Personas are excluded from editorial and algorithmic recommendations, unless a listener follows one, Spotify said.

The company has also introduced a beta programme called Artist Profile Protection, which allows musicians to review releases uploaded under their names and guard against impersonation and stream-farming.

As AI-generated music becomes more popular, Spotify’s efforts to identify and remove spam are likely to remain an ongoing challenge.

Features

Trump targets Ilhan Omar over Somali roots. ‘It’s got no government, no police protection’.

Trump’s remarks come after Homeland Security Investigations and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raided Omar’s residence in Washington, D.C., on 12 October.

Manisha Mondal

21 October, 2026 01:12 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Trump also made disparaging comments about Somalia, where Omar was born / Commons; Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Ahead of the US midterm elections in November, President Donald Trump has attacked Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, questioning her loyalty to the United States and suggesting she could face jail or deportation to Somalia.

On Tuesday, October 20, Trump called Omar “a sick and a very dishonest person” and claimed she “hates our country”.

“She could also go to jail. You know, they keep talking about deportation. No, she could go to jail. This is just my opinion,” Trump said, while addressing a press conference at the White House.

Show Full Article

Hours later, Omar, who has been reportedly absent from public life for the past few days, uploaded a video message on Instagram, thanking all her supporters for campaign donations. “We are not going to be intimidated,” she added, responding to Trump’s remarks.

She also vowed to continue campaigning ahead of the midterms, saying she would work to defeat Republicans, win control of both the House and Senate, and hold the Trump administration accountable.

Trump attacks Omar over her Somali roots During his remarks on Tuesday, Trump also made disparaging comments about Somalia, where Omar was born.

“She comes from a country that’s essentially not even a country — Somalia,” he said, claiming the country lacked a functioning government and police force.

“All they do is have people running around shooting each other, then she comes over here,” Trump said, adding that Omar was attempting to tell Americans how to run their country despite coming from Somalia.

“She never even heard the word constitution,” he added. He also called the congresswoman “a disgrace to our country.”

Also Read: US immigration authorities raid home of Democratic Trump critic Ilhan Omar

Federal agents search Omar’s home Trump’s remarks come after Homeland Security Investigations and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raided Omar’s residence in Washington, D.C., on 12 October.

According to Reuters , the investigation concerns whether Omar or her relatives provided false information in immigration paperwork when her family arrived in the US as refugees in the 1990s or during the process of obtaining citizenship.

No finding of wrongdoing has been announced, and Omar has denied the allegations.

Following the search, she said on X that Trump had targeted her with “baseless lies and smear campaigns” for a decade, adding, “I will not be silenced.”

Omar arrived in the US with her family in 1995 after fleeing Somalia’s civil war and became a naturalised US citizen in 2000. She was first elected to the US House of Representatives in 2018 and took office in January 2019. She represents Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District.

(Edited by Maryam Hassan)
